proposals.before: His father Fu had passed the jinshi examination in 1801; starting as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy, he rose to vice minister of rites, was honored with a second senior graduates' banquet, and was made junior guardian of the heir apparent. When he died he was posthumously ennobled as grand tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.
proposals.after: His father E had passed the jinshi examination in 1801; starting as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy, he rose to vice minister of rites, was honored with a second senior graduates' banquet, and was made junior guardian of the heir apparent. When he died he was posthumously ennobled as grand tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 堮 is Du E, not Fu; the English personal name is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: His father Fu was a jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing; from Hanlin compiler he rose in succession to Vice Minister of Rites, was granted a second Deer-Ming banquet, appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and upon death was posthumously given Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenduan.
proposals.after: His father E was a jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing; from Hanlin compiler he rose in succession to Vice Minister of Rites, was granted a second Deer-Ming banquet, appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and upon death was posthumously given Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenduan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 堮 is Du E, not Fu; the literal English personal name is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: Xianfeng was stricken: he posthumously made Shoutian grand tutor and grand secretary, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, gave five thousand taels for the funeral, sent a close minister to console his father Fu, promoted his son Han from reviewer to chamberlain of the heir apparent, and granted all three grandsons the juren degree.
proposals.after: Xianfeng was stricken: he posthumously made Shoutian grand tutor and grand secretary, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, gave five thousand taels for the funeral, sent a close minister to console his father E, promoted his son Han from reviewer to chamberlain of the heir apparent, and granted all three grandsons the juren degree.
proposals.reason: Chinese 堮 is Du E; English Fu is a mistransliteration carried from s0002.

proposals.before: Wenzong was deeply grieved; he posthumously granted Grand Tutor and Grand Secretary, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, granted five thousand taels for the funeral, sent a close official to comfort his father Fu, promoted his son the compiler Han to chamberlain for the heir, and granted all three grandsons the status of provincial graduates.
proposals.after: Wenzong was deeply grieved; he posthumously granted Grand Tutor and Grand Secretary, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, granted five thousand taels for the funeral, sent a close official to comfort his father E, promoted his son the compiler Han to chamberlain for the heir, and granted all three grandsons the status of provincial graduates.
proposals.reason: Chinese 堮 is Du E; English Fu is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: When the coffin reached Beijing the emperor sacrificed in person, stroked the bier, and wept bitterly, and raised his father Fu with the honorary rank of minister of rites.
proposals.after: When the coffin reached Beijing the emperor sacrificed in person, stroked the bier, and wept bitterly, and raised his father E with the honorary rank of minister of rites.
proposals.reason: Chinese 堮 is Du E; English Fu is a mistransliteration carried from s0002.

proposals.before: When the coffin reached the capital, the emperor personally offered sacrifice, caressed the coffin and wept bitterly, and promoted his father Fu with the nominal rank of Minister of Rites.
proposals.after: When the coffin reached the capital, the emperor personally offered sacrifice, caressed the coffin and wept bitterly, and promoted his father E with the nominal rank of Minister of Rites.
proposals.reason: Chinese 堮 is Du E; English Fu is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: Censor Dong Yuanchun asked that the two empress dowagers rule from behind a screen; Zaiyuan, Duhua, Sushun, and their party objected; Han sided with them and argued fiercely, and Dong's proposal was set aside.
proposals.after: Censor Dong Yuanchun asked that the two empress dowagers rule from behind a screen; Zaiyuan, Duanhua, Sushun, and their party objected; Han sided with them and argued fiercely, and Dong's proposal was set aside.
proposals.reason: Chinese 端華 is Duanhua; Duhua omits the medial an.

proposals.before: Censor Dong Yuanchun memorialized asking the two empress dowagers to attend court behind the curtain; Zaiyuan, Duhua, Sushun and others objected; Han sided with them and argued forcefully, so Dong's proposal was rejected.
proposals.after: Censor Dong Yuanchun memorialized asking the two empress dowagers to attend court behind the curtain; Zaiyuan, Duanhua, Sushun and others objected; Han sided with them and argued forcefully, so Dong's proposal was rejected.
proposals.reason: Chinese 端華 is Duanhua; Duhua omits the medial an.

proposals.before: he also impeached Wenzhou prefect Liu Yu for botching a ticket-salt trial, was himself censured, protested injustice, and was sent to Xinjiang.
proposals.after: he also impeached Wenzhou prefect Liu Yu for botching a ticket-salt trial; Liu Yu was censured, protested injustice, and was sent to Xinjiang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 被議…戍新疆 continues the object 劉煜, not the impeaching subject Qi Junzao, who remains in office afterward.

proposals.before: he also impeached Wenzhou prefect Liu Yu for mishandling the ticket-salt trial and was himself censured; he submitted that he had been wronged and was banished to Xinjiang.
proposals.after: he also impeached Wenzhou prefect Liu Yu for mishandling the ticket-salt trial; Liu Yu was censured, submitted that he had been wronged, and was banished to Xinjiang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 被議…戍新疆 refers to Liu Yu (劉煜), not Qi Junzao.

proposals.before: When Zeng Guofan's Hunan Army was new, Sushun urged employing it and the emperor agreed; Junzao disagreed on every front, often pleaded illness to quit, and was warmly urged to remain.
proposals.after: When the Hunan Army was new, Sushun urged employing it and the emperor agreed; Junzao disagreed on every front, often pleaded illness to quit, and was warmly urged to remain.
proposals.reason: Chinese names only 湘軍; Zeng Guofan is not in the source and should not be invented.

proposals.before: In 1884 he and Minister Yanchi inspected Shandong river works and wrote: "Without opening the sea mouth the flood cannot be released.
proposals.after: In 1884 he and Minister Yan Xu inspected Shandong river works and wrote: "Without opening the sea mouth the flood cannot be released.
proposals.reason: 延煦 is Yan Xu; Yanchi wrongly romanizes 煦.

proposals.before: In the tenth year he was ordered together with Minister Yanchi to investigate Shandong river works, memorializing: 'Without dredging the sea mouth the great flood cannot be discharged.
proposals.after: In the tenth year he was ordered together with Minister Yan Xu to investigate Shandong river works, memorializing: 'Without dredging the sea mouth the great flood cannot be discharged.
proposals.reason: 延煦 is Yan Xu; Yanchi misreads 煦.

proposals.before: His grandson Shizeng was made an outer-office secretary; his son You an inner-office secretary.
proposals.after: His grandson Shizeng was made an outer-office secretary; his son Youmeng an inner-office secretary.
proposals.reason: Chinese 友蒙 is Youmeng; English drops 蒙.

proposals.before: His grandson Shizeng was granted secretary in the outer office; his son You was granted secretary in the inner office.
proposals.after: His grandson Shizeng was granted secretary in the outer office; his son Youmeng was granted secretary in the inner office.
proposals.reason: Chinese 友蒙 is Youmeng; You omits 蒙.

proposals.before: crush Nian bandits in Shandong, Henan, Anhui, and Henan before they joined the Taiping;
proposals.after: crush Nian bandits in Yan, Yu, Feng, and Ying before they joined the Taiping;
proposals.reason: 兗豫鳳潁 are Yan, Yu, Feng, Ying; idiomatic repeats Henan.

proposals.before: He rose through director, vice minister of sacrifices and of imperial entertainments, Shuntian vice governor, transmission vice commissioner, and imperial clan vice director.
proposals.after: He rose through director, vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and of imperial entertainments, Shuntian vice governor, transmission vice commissioner, and imperial clan vice director.
proposals.reason: 鴻臚寺 is the Court of State Ceremonial (Honglu Temple), not a court of sacrifices; 'sacrifices' mistranslates 鴻臚寺.

proposals.before: He was promoted in succession to director, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, vice governor of Shuntian, vice commissioner of the Transmission Office, and vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
proposals.after: He was promoted in succession to director, vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, vice governor of Shuntian, vice commissioner of the Transmission Office, and vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
proposals.reason: 鴻臚寺 is not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (太常寺); literal English misidentifies the office.

proposals.before: In 1851 he was ordered to serve above the Grand Councilors.
proposals.after: In 1851 he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council in the capacity of a Grand Councilor.
proposals.reason: 在軍機大臣上行走 is the Qing appointment formula for serving as a Grand Councilor, not literally 'above' the ministers.

proposals.before: In the first year of Xianfeng he was ordered to serve above the Grand Council ministers.
proposals.after: In the first year of Xianfeng he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council in the capacity of a Grand Council minister.
proposals.reason: Calque of 上 as 'above' obscures the standard office formula 在軍機大臣上行走.

proposals.before: He asked that Zeng Guofan send able commanders to Tongzhou and Dongtai to rally morale, spur loyal militia, advance on Suzhou and Changzhou, and hold the lower Yangzi.
proposals.after: He asked that Zeng Guofan send able commanders to Tongzhou and Dongtai to rally morale, spur loyal militia, advance on Suzhou and Changzhou, and fall back to guard the Lixiahe (lower-river) region.
proposals.reason: 下河 denotes the Lixiahe region north of the Yangzi, not generically 'the lower Yangzi'.

proposals.before: He Guiqing of Liangjiang was clever and self-confident; Yunzhang wrongly praised him repeatedly to the throne.
proposals.after: Liangjiang Governor-General He Guiqing was clever and self-confident; Yunzhang wrongly praised him repeatedly to the throne.
proposals.reason: Chinese 兩江總督何桂清 names his office as Liangjiang Governor-General; the idiomatic omits 總督.

proposals.before: In 1861, recovered, he acted as war minister and then left censor-in-chief.
proposals.after: In 1861, recovered, he acted as Minister of War, and soon also acted as Left Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尋兼署左都御史 means he soon concurrently acted as Left Censor-in-Chief; 'then left' reverses 兼署.

decisions.reason: s0002 opens 父堮; 堮 is read E, so Fu is a mistransliteration, and replacing only that name restores the Chinese personal name without other changes.
The same 父堮 stands in the literal English as Fu; E matches the given name while the rest already tracks 嘉慶六年進士…諡文端.
s0027 has 慰視其父堮; Fu again misreads 堮, and E is the accurate given name in an otherwise faithful idiomatic sentence.
The literal likewise names 其父堮 as Fu; correcting to E restores the Chinese personal name without inventing other content.
s0033 ends 晉其父堮禮部尚書銜; Fu is the same misreading of 堮, and E is the correct replacement.
The literal repeats Fu for 其父堮; E matches the Chinese name and leaves the honorary 禮部尚書銜 wording intact.
s0045 lists 載垣、端華、肅順; 端華 is Duanhua, so Duhua drops the medial an and the proposed fix is exact.
The literal has the same Duhua for 端華; Duanhua is the standard reading and the rest of the sentence already tracks the Chinese.
After 又劾溫州知府劉煜…不善, 被議，自呈枉屈，戍新疆 continues that object; s0064 still has Junzao on duty, so the banishment belongs to Liu Yu, not the impeacher.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又劾溫州知府劉煜試行票鹽不善，被議，自呈枉屈，戍新疆

decisions.reason: The literal wrongly makes the impeacher the patient of 被議…戍新疆; renaming the censured actor as Liu Yu matches the Chinese object and the following units.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 劉煜試行票鹽不善，被議，自呈枉屈，戍新疆

decisions.reason: s0077 names only 湘軍初起; Zeng Guofan is not in the Chinese and the proposed deletion removes invented attribution without other loss.
s0133 has 尚書延煦; 煦 is xu, so Yanchi misreads the given name and Yan Xu restores it.
The literal likewise writes Yanchi for 延煦; Yan Xu is the accurate romanization and leaves the memorial wording unchanged.
s0143 grants office to 子友蒙; You truncates 友蒙, and Youmeng restores the full given name.
The literal also shortens 友蒙 to You; Youmeng matches the Chinese personal name without further rewriting.
s0163 lists 兗、豫、鳳、潁; the before text invents a duplicated Henan sequence, while Yan, Yu, Feng, and Ying track the four place names and remove the error.
s0221 has 鴻臚寺少卿; 鴻臚寺 is the Court of State Ceremonial, not a sacrifices office (太常寺), so the proposed title correction is required.
The literal's Court of Imperial Sacrifices misidentifies 鴻臚寺; Court of State Ceremonial is the accurate office name and the remaining posts already match.
命在軍機大臣上行走 is the Qing formula for appointment to serve as a Grand Councilor; 'above the Grand Councilors' is a false calque of 上.
The literal calques the same 上 as 'above'; rendering the formula as service on the Grand Council in a Grand Council minister's capacity restores the office sense.
s0208 ends 進搗蘇、常，退保下河; 下河 is the Lixiahe/lower-river region, not a generic lower Yangzi, and the repair also restores the 退保 'fall back to guard' sense lost in 'hold'.
s0246 opens 兩江總督何桂清; the before text keeps the person and place but drops 總督, and naming him Liangjiang Governor-General restores the office.
署兵部尚書，尋兼署左都御史 marks concurrent acting as Left Censor-in-Chief; 'then left' erases 兼署, and the proposed wording restores both the titles and the concurrency.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 署兵部尚書，尋兼署左都御史

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0007 shows the English name Duhua was produced only by misreading 端華; s0045 supports Duanhua (c0073), not a separate Duhua alias.
Accepted r0012 shows Yanchi arose only from misreading 延煦; s0133 supports Yan Xu (c0193), not a separate Yanchi name.
